Light does not bend when the incident ray is along the normal line.
Light bends toward the normal when entering a denser medium from a less dense medium.
Light bends away from the normal when entering a less dense medium from a denser medium.
The angle of incidence is greater than the angle of refraction when light enters a denser
The angle of incidence is less than the angle of refraction when light enters a less dense
As the angle of incidence increases, the angle of refraction also increases.
The speed of light decreases when it enters a denser transparent medium.
Some light is partially reflected at transparent surfaces, reducing transmitted intensity.
